description: A sunset painting of a large domed city with a tall spiral-banded minaret, glazed turquoise and gold tilework, arched gateways, walls and smaller domes. A winding river runs across flat land with small boats on it; in the foreground a camel caravan and two horse riders cross the riverbank. The sky is orange, pink and purple. The painting fills the frame edge to edge with no border; no readable letters or numbers, only a small white sparkle logo in the bottom-right corner.
reason: Shows a glazed-tile Islamic city with a spiral minaret and domes, not the Roman-era writer or his novel; the card is Apuleius writing The Golden Ass in 170 CE. Redraw as a 2nd-century Roman scene (a writer, a book roll, or a Roman North African town) with no Islamic domes or minarets.
